page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with a two-line Syriac heading at the top, full width. No margin notes. The right edge of the scan cuts off the ends of several lines. Catchword at the lower right.

main_text.head: [illegible, ~14 letters] [illegible, ~12 letters]
De diebus obdormientium, siue Defunctorum & qui sunt absoluendi: Iacobi.
main_text.p: Oftendimus etiam ibidem ex auctoritate, ac testimonio Ioannis Episcopi Darensis, Scriptoris celeberrimi 4. saeculi a Christo Domino apud Syros, animas Defunctorum leuiori-bus delictis, & sordibus coinquinatas igne Purgatorio purgari. Quam quidem tam vetusti Scriptoris auctoritatem, vt quae plurimum pungit, & vrget latera Hottin-geri impudentissime afferentis, ac ferrea fronte pronunciantis, Nullam plane in Syrorum Symbolicis Scriptis Purgatorij mentionem esse, hic iterum repetere non pigebit, vt videant inde, qui ab eius stant partibus, qualem meretur in reliquis fidem. Verba ipsissima sunt ex lib. 4. De Resurrectione Mortuorum cap. 24. Si lenibus alis, inquit, predita est anima, in suo discessu ad illum, qui eam attraxit, in laetitia erit perfecta; si vero onus passionum gestat, afflictionem patitur, non quod odit, aut vlciscitur Creator, sed vt ad se attrahat PVRIFICATAM; Quemadmodum materiam, quae commixta est auro, in ignem immittunt, vt purificetur, quae confusa ini-

page.notes: The scan is cropped at the right edge, so the final letters of several lines are missing (for example after "in_" and "qui", "ac", "Creator"). I have not reconstructed them. The Syriac heading is not legible enough to transcribe; the placeholders give only approximate letter counts. The line "Verba ipsissima" begins flush left, and I have treated the passage as one paragraph because no indent is visible. Long s is printed as f throughout, and I have normalised it to s, for example "Oftendimus", "teftimonio", "Chrifto", "ipfiffima".
